name: dForce LPCurveGaugeAggregatorModel read-only reentrancy
summary: LPCurveBaseAggregatorModel._getPrice(), the code behind dForce's wstETHCRV-gauge vault aggregator, prices the collateral as priceOracle.getUnderlyingPrice(pool.coins(0)) * pool.get_virtual_price(). get_virtual_price() is an unguarded external view on the Curve ETH/wstETH pool 0x6eb2dc694eb516b16dc9fbc678c60052bbdd7d80 and returns D * PRECISION / token_supply, so while remove_liquidity() is paying out native ETH through raw_call the LP supply has already been reduced but the balances have not fully settled and the ratio is wrong. The aggregator performs the read with no reentrancy probe, so re-entering from the pool's ETH refund let the attacker have dForce value the vwstETHCRV-gauge collateral at a distorted price, seize a 1,019.577317265394873995 gauge-token position and mint 1,219,437.439363481229905117 USX of unbacked debt in the same transaction.
notes: LPCurveGaugeAggregatorModel is a plain non-proxy contract with no DELEGATECALL in its runtime. Its runtime is byte-identical at the creation block, at the block before the exploit, and today, so the executed pricing code dates from deployment two days and 13 hours earlier.

Both components are measured from the anchor receipt. The vwstETHCRV-gauge market 0x2ce498b79c499c6bb64934042eba487bd31f75ea held 1,048.408829854823855419 gauge tokens at block 59527633 and 28.831512589428981424 at block 59527634, and its iToken supply falls by the same 1,019.577317265394873995 at an exchange rate of exactly 1e18, all of it taken from depositor 0x916792f7734089470de27297903bed8a4630b26d. The gauge token is valued the way dForce's own aggregator values it outside reentrancy: get_virtual_price 1.011371298035750307 at block 59527633 times the DefiLlama ETH price 1544.78, i.e. 1562.3461537796664 USD, giving 1,031.17 ETH-equivalent, which matches dForce's own public figure of 1,031.42 ETH liquidated on Arbitrum. USX net minted in the transaction is 1,219,437.439363481229905117 (mints minus burns against the zero address) and is valued at par; dForce publicly put the protocol debt created across both chains at 2.3 million USD, of which this Arbitrum leg is 1.22 million. Cross-check on the attacker side: the attacker EOA's native balance rises by exactly 1,236.654369923464 ETH in this transaction and it also keeps 719,437.439363481229905117 USX, the remaining 500,000 USX having been swapped to 493,757.29376 USDC.e and then to WETH inside the transaction; realised proceeds are slightly below gross depletion because of flash-loan and swap costs. Attacker-supplied capital was 0.5 ETH staged in transaction 0x5f238693 and is not deducted from these victim-side figures. Aave, Balancer and Uniswap V3 flash loans are repaid within the transaction and are not loss. The attacker returned 1,237 ETH to dForce on 2023-02-13; per methodology that later recovery does not reduce gross depletion. The same-day Optimism campaign against the mirror deployment (exploit 0x6c19762186c9f32c81eb2a79420fc7ad4485aa916cab37ec278b216757bfba0d) is a separate incident and none of its loss is counted here.

The gauge-token component is valued with the Curve pool's own pre-exploit virtual price times the DefiLlama ETH price rather than a market quote, because wstETHCRV-gauge has no third-party price feed. The resulting 1,031.17 ETH-equivalent agrees with dForce's own published figure of 1,031.42 ETH.
USX is dForce's own stablecoin. It is valued at par here; DefiLlama quoted 1.035 at the anchor timestamp while the attacker's own disposals realised about 0.97, so par sits between the two marks.
